analysis.investment_thesis: Srigee DLM fails the Magic Formula test decisively — while the P/E of 9.46 looks superficially cheap, a ROE of just 0.30% signals a business generating essentially zero return on capital. Cheap + bad = value trap, not a Magic Formula candidate.
key_strengths: Low headline P/E of 9.46x suggests modest earnings yield
Promoter holding at 45.23% provides some alignment
Plastic OEM/ODM niche with design-led positioning
key_risks: ROE of 0.30% implies near-zero return on capital — disqualifying
Tiny INR 38 Cr market cap = illiquid microcap with BSE-only listing
Capital-intensive plastic manufacturing with no evidence of ROIC moat
red_flags: ROE 0.30% is catastrophically low — fails ROC half of Magic Formula
Sub-50% promoter holding in a microcap raises control/skin-in-game concerns
No EBIT/EV data disclosed to verify true earnings yield
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The Magic Formula ranks companies on two axes: earnings yield (cheapness) and return on capital (quality). Srigee DLM fails catastrophically on the second axis — a 0.30% ROE means the business is generating virtually no return on shareholder capital, which almost certainly implies ROIC well below any reasonable cost of capital. The 9.46x P/E is meaningless in this context because low-quality earnings compounding at ~0% destroy value regardless of entry multiple. This is the textbook value trap my formula is designed to avoid.

Even if I gave full benefit of the doubt on earnings yield (say 10-11%), pairing it with near-zero ROC puts this stock in the bottom decile of the combined ranking. Plastic OEM/ODM is a commodity contract-manufacturing business with pricing pressure from customers and input-cost volatility from crude derivatives — structural reasons why ROIC stays compressed. At INR 38 Cr market cap with thin institutional coverage (FII 2.25%, DII 0%), there's no catalyst visibility either. Pass — the Magic Formula says buy good businesses at fair prices, not mediocre businesses at cheap ones.
